findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the database data and backups are stored without encryption at rest, exposing sensitive data if storage is compromised.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the RDS instance to the public internet rather than confining it to the private network.

lifecycle ignore_changes = ["password"] means Terraform will not detect or remediate password drift, allowing the administrative password to be changed outside of IaC control without enforcement of the configured password.
Egress rule allows all traffic (protocol -1, ports 0-0) to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting the database to reach any external host, which can be abused for data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.

The EC2 role policy grants wildcard actions across s3, ec2, and rds on all resources ("*"), far exceeding least privilege and allowing the instance to read/write any S3 data, perform arbitrary EC2 operations, and manage all RDS instances.

user_data embeds the database password in plaintext (define('DB_PASSWORD', '${var.password}')), leaking the credential into instance user data where it is visible in the EC2 console and API, and permitting full database access from the compromised instance.

The web app connects to MySQL without TLS and the instance is used by the EC2 app over the public network, transmitting DB credentials and data in cleartext; no requiring_ssl parameter or encrypted transport is configured.

The database ingress is open to the entire VPC CIDR, and combined with publicly_accessible the DB can be reached beyond the intended applications; access lacks the principle of least privilege at the network layer.
